source.title: Representation Based Complexity Measures for Predicting Generalization in Deep Learning

record.tranche_reason: The study compares post-hoc complexity measures by how much information they provide about the generalization gap, using a different set of measures and a conditional mutual-information score.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports mutual-information scores for complexity measures on CIFAR-10 and SVHN. The paper also discusses cited results and design choices; those are not separate rows.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates post-hoc generalization predictors, but does not establish a test of any listed version. Its Sharpness baseline is not identified as magnitude-aware, and Section 5 says some baseline scores are taken from Jiang et al. rather than independently measured here. Hyperparameter variation alone supplies no width, batch-size, or dropout intervention results.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate, but should say the proposed measures can outperform the reported baselines, rather than implying consistent superiority. The authors argue that representation consistency, robustness, and separability predict generalization gaps across varied architectures and hyperparameters. Their results concern predictive association, without establishing that improving these properties causally improves generalization.
record.recipe_differences: Post-hoc comparison of representation-based complexity measures and baselines on competition models; it does not reproduce the interventions or measurements in the listed original studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Scores vary by dataset and by complexity measure; the paper notes that layer choice and other design choices affect scores.

fits_no_version.finding: Representation-based predictors receive dataset- and design-dependent conditional mutual-information scores. For example, generic DBI scores are 1.76 and 7.98, whereas task-specialized variants score 25.22 and 22.19 on CIFAR-10 and SVHN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-hoc representation measures can predict differences in generalization gaps, with predictive performance depending on dataset, layer, augmentation, and measure.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 compares representation predictors with norm, unspecified sharpness, and VC-dimension baselines; it does not identify a magnitude-aware sharpness test.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some representation-based predictors outperform the reported baseline predictors on these PGDL tasks.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS Competition on Predicting Generalization in Deep Learning (NeurIPS 2020)
record.problems: Results are principally aggregate conditional mutual-information scores; the paper does not report uncertainty for those scores in Table 1, nor direct per-model training-test gap values there. The sharpness baseline is not identified as magnitude-aware.

untested.parts: No empirical comparison of random-label fitting, random-label held-out accuracy, and natural-label held-out accuracy. Figure 2 is a schematic argument.
No test-error trajectory as width increases beyond interpolation.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No optimizer comparison under specified tuning budgets.
No held-out-performance comparison across batch sizes with epoch budgets controlled.
No held-out-error comparison with and without dropout.
The unspecified Sharpness baseline does not identify magnitude-aware perturbations or establish their directional relationship with the gap and ranking against norm and margin measures.
No removal and retraining experiment comparing memorized examples with random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Section 5 describes 150 public models across CIFAR-10 and SVHN; it does not establish 150 models for each dataset. Apply that subject correction throughout. Tables 2 and 3 add predictor-performance results on other PGDL tasks, but no missing test of V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not tested.
No width sweep around the interpolation threshold is reported.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison is reported.
No dropout intervention comparison is reported.
The study reports a baseline called Sharpness, but does not specify magnitude-aware weight perturbations or test the stated relation among similarly low-training-loss networks.
No memorized-example removal experiment is reported.
